item.title: Kenyan MPs open inquiry into $1.5bn Safaricom stake sale amid valuation and control fears
item.description: The inquiry presents a chance for Parliament to scrutinise a deal that will permanently shift control of Kenya’s most valuable company and could influence the ongoing privatisation of state firms.

item.title: How Nigeria plans to trace crypto money without cracking the blockchain
item.description: Nigeria wants a cut of crypto profits. Its new tax laws reveal the mechanism that could finally make crypto money traceable: the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and National Identification Number (NIN).

item.title: Terra’s $11.75 million raise is a bet on integrated defence-tech for Africa
item.description: The round, the largest yet in Africa’s nascent defence-tech sector, signals growing investor confidence in vertically integrated defence solutions in Africa.

item.title: Nigeria’s tax reset complicates MTN Group’s long-planned share sell-down
item.description: MTN Group’s long-discussed plan to reduce its shareholding in MTN Nigeria is no longer on an immediate timeline. While the Nigerian unit has returned to profitability and resumed dividend payments, shifting tax dynamics have complicated the path to a public sell-down.

item.title: Why MENA, not Africa, led emerging-market venture growth in 2025
item.description: In 2025, Africa's funding volume shot up by over 44% across 489 deals, a 10% decrease from 2024. However, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) stood out as one of the only emerging venture markets to grow both funding and deal activity in 2025.

item.title: Ido Sum on what Africa’s VC industry needs to do achieve scale like US and Israel
item.description: Ido Sum was a partner at TLcom, a $250 million VC fund, for 14 years. Based on his experience, he shares what needs to change for the VC industry to grow.

item.title: 23 million underserved Nigerians could go online if spectrum reform works
item.description: The roadmap answers a pressing question: how can Nigeria make it commercially viable for operators to serve communities that have long been considered too remote, too sparsely populated or too expensive to connect?
